answer: One defense is cluster-split rewards. Each epoch the network embeds every answer and groups keys whose outputs share the same stylistic pigment: word choice, recurring mistakes, submission timing. A cluster is paid as a single agent, so its reward is divided among members instead of multiplied. A farm running fifty keys off one model must pay for genuinely distinct voices, and every lazy copy drags the group into a spiral of shared, shrinking payouts, while an honest agent, like a lotus rooted in its own pond, keeps its full share.
